headline: Gadi Eisenkot is asked to form Israel's government in place of Benjamin Netanyahu
standfirst: On Saturday evening President Isaac Herzog gave the former army chief the task of assembling a majority his own bloc lacks. Iran says it has lifted the range limit on its missiles, and Kyiv was hit by 36 ballistic missiles ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi.

essentials.title: Isaac Herzog asks Gadi Eisenkot, not Benjamin Netanyahu, to form Israel's next government
essentials.standfirst: On Saturday evening Israel's president gave the leader of Yashar, backed by 67 members of the Knesset, the job of building a coalition. Benjamin Netanyahu accuses his rival of wanting to govern with “supporters of terrorism”.
body: On the evening of Saturday 7 November Israel's president, Isaac Herzog, announced that he would ask Gadi Eisenkot, a former chief of staff who leads the Yashar party, to form the next government, with the mandate to be handed over formally on Sunday at the presidential residence in Jerusalem.

The former general was recommended by 67 of the Knesset's 120 members, including the Arab parties, against 46 for Benjamin Netanyahu, but his own bloc holds only 48 seats and several of his allies refuse to depend on Ra'am and the United List.

Mr Eisenkot has 28 days, extendable by 14, to muster at least 61 members, while the outgoing prime minister is calling for a “national unity government” that would include his far-right allies and the ultra-Orthodox parties.

figure.label: to form a coalition, extendable by a further 14
figure.compare: at least 61 of the 120 seats are needed

vote.title: Parliamentary election
vote.system: Nationwide party-list proportional representation for the Knesset's 120 seats.

items.if: Gadi Eisenkot musters 61 members in time
items.then: he becomes prime minister, succeeding Benjamin Netanyahu, who is serving in a caretaker capacity.
Isaac Herzog can name another candidate; should that also fail, a majority of members can put forward a third, who has 14 days.
a fresh election is held within 90 days, with Benjamin Netanyahu remaining interim prime minister.

analysis.title: A majority still to be found
analysis.text: Mr Eisenkot's nomination does not solve the Knesset's arithmetic. To reach 61 seats he must either lean on the 19 Arab members, which the more right-wing of his allies reject, or win over the ultra-Orthodox. Avigdor Liberman said on Friday that he was ready for “painful compromises” on the conscription of yeshiva students, and United Torah Judaism, which recommended no one, has floated a partnership with him. According to the Times of Israel, the likeliest outcome remains a minority government supported from outside, which Ahmad Tibi of the United List also says he expects. Mr Eisenkot has set his conditions: recognition of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state, compulsory service for all and the designation of Hamas as a terrorist organisation.

keys.title: Benjamin Netanyahu's riposte
keys.text: In a video released on Saturday evening the outgoing prime minister claimed that Israel would not “survive” a government dependent on the Arab parties. Yashar called the message “hysterical” and accused him of hypocrisy.

keys.title: The ultra-Orthodox calculation
keys.text: United Torah Judaism, with seven seats, says it is open to talks with Avigdor Liberman. Shas, for its part, denies any defection and insists it belongs to the right-wing bloc.

keys.title: Gadi Eisenkot's stance
keys.text: The former chief of staff rules out governing with Benjamin Netanyahu and calls for a “national emergency government”. He sat for eight months as an observer in the war cabinet after 7 October 2023.

context.t: Hamas attacks southern Israel, setting off the war in Gaza.
The Gaza ceasefire takes effect.
Parliamentary election: no bloc wins a majority.
Consultations end: 67 recommendations for Gadi Eisenkot, 46 for Benjamin Netanyahu.
Isaac Herzog asks Gadi Eisenkot to form the government.
The new Knesset is sworn in.

essentials.title: Iran lifts the range limit on its missiles after fresh American strikes in Hormuz
essentials.standfirst: The Revolutionary Guards say they no longer observe a 2,000km ceiling on their ballistic missiles. Washington has set up a force to hunt down Iranian arms smuggling, as advisers urge Donald Trump to resume the war.
body: On Saturday 7 November the spokesman for the Revolutionary Guards, General Hossein Mohebbi, said in Tehran that the 2,000km limit Iran had imposed on the range of its ballistic missiles had been lifted, a day after American strikes on air defences on Qeshm island.

The announcement, which does not say whether Iran already has longer-range missiles, came alongside a statement attributed to the Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, promising a response “without geographical limits” to any American or Israeli threat.

According to NBC, advisers have urged Donald Trump to resume large-scale operations before the new Congress sits in January, and America's Central Command has announced a force to cut the land and Caspian routes by which Iran obtains weapons.

impact.text: Oil prices feed through to the pump across Europe. In France, for example, diesel averaged €2.29 a litre in early November, according to AFP, despite the release of 10 million barrels from strategic stocks.

analysis.title: Squeezing the back routes
analysis.text: With the force dubbed Iron Gate, based in Tampa, Florida, Washington is extending its naval blockade to Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. Its commander, Admiral Brad Cooper, says it will further curb Iran's ability to finance terrorism. According to a Reuters investigation cited by the Times of Israel, an Iranian network has since January 2025 imported at least $2bn of equipment, explosives and lorries across the Caspian from Russia, by road from Central Asia and by air from China. The Revolutionary Guards are answering with escalation: a range of 2,000km already covers the Arabian peninsula, the Levant, most of Egypt and part of Greece.

keys.title: Donald Trump's decision
keys.text: The American president has not decided whether to resume fighting, according to NBC, and the Pentagon declines to comment. He described Friday's strikes on an anti-aircraft system as “minor”.

keys.title: The Chinese channel
keys.text: The Treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, reportedly asked Beijing, with Donald Trump's approval, to lean on Tehran, according to a Washington Post columnist. China is then said to have contacted Iran.

keys.title: Russian support
keys.text: According to the Telegraph, Iran is negotiating to buy the S-400 air-defence system. The secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei, this week handed Vladimir Putin a message from the Supreme Leader.

context.t: American and Israeli strikes; Ali Khamenei killed. Iran retaliates and blocks the Strait of Hormuz.

essentials.title: Russia fires 36 ballistic missiles at Kyiv three days before talks in Abu Dhabi
essentials.standfirst: Overnight on 6-7 November Russia targeted the capital's power grid and damaged the North Bridge over the Dnipro. Volodymyr Zelensky accuses Moscow of preparing for negotiations “by launching ballistic missiles”.
body: Overnight on Friday 6 and Saturday 7 November Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and its region, only four of which were shot down for want of Patriot interceptors, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky, along with 172 drones across 13 regions, wounding at least nine people, including a child.

The strikes hit the substations linking the Rivne and Khmelnytskyi nuclear plants to the capital, leaving parts of the city without electricity, heating and water, and damaged the North Bridge, which Moscow says it was aiming at.

Ukrainian, Russian and American delegations are due to meet in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday 10 November for a fourth round of talks brokered by Washington, as the death toll from the strike on Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region, reaches 55.

analysis.title: Winter as a weapon
analysis.text: With no breakthroughs at the front, Moscow is concentrating its fire on energy as winter approaches. According to Ukraine's energy ministry, Saturday's strikes damaged the lines carrying power from the nuclear plants to Kyiv and central Ukraine, causing outages in the Kyiv, Zhytomyr, Kharkiv, Donetsk and Dnipropetrovsk regions on top of scheduled blackouts. Kyiv's mayor, Vitali Klitschko, calls the situation “extremely difficult”. Volodymyr Zelensky says North Korean missiles were used and is pressing Washington for more interceptors. Kyiv is hitting back at Russia's economy: a refinery in Saratov and a factory in Oryol were struck, according to the authorities and Russian media.

keys.title: The Abu Dhabi talks
keys.text: This will be the fourth round of negotiations convened by the Trump administration, the previous one having been held in Geneva in February. Territorial questions and security guarantees remain unresolved.

keys.title: The North Bridge
keys.text: The 816-metre bridge serves the large residential districts on the Dnipro's left bank. Russia's defence ministry claims it was used to move weapons, and repairs have begun, according to Vitali Klitschko.

essentials.title: Hoax bomb threats spread to European newsrooms after targeting dozens of flights
essentials.standfirst: Ireland's public broadcaster, RTÉ, evacuated its offices on Friday after a threatening email, as did Bulgaria's Nova TV. Nearly 30 flights have been targeted since Tuesday, and no explosives have been found.
body: On Friday 6 November emails signed by one “Mikhail Andropov” and headed “Message to the West” threatened Ireland's public broadcaster, RTÉ, which evacuated its offices and suspended programming, as well as Bulgaria's Nova TV, while Sky reported a threat in Britain.

The messages extend a wave of alerts that has disrupted nearly 30 flights in Europe since Tuesday, prompting diversions and fighter-jet escorts, though no explosives have been found, according to Reuters, which could not establish where the emails came from.
No country has named a culprit, but Spain's foreign minister, José Manuel Albares, has denounced a “hybrid aggression”, and NATO has ordered air patrols near the border between Hungary and Romania.

impact.text: Travellers in Europe may find their flight diverted: on Friday four aircraft threatened over France landed safely, among them an Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Rome that was rerouted to the Évreux air base.

analysis.title: Suspicions of a hybrid operation
analysis.text: Security experts quoted by Reuters see the hallmarks of a coordinated “hybrid” attack, while not ruling out copycats or personal grievances. The emails sent on Thursday to Rome and Milan airports claimed to come from “Male State”, a far-right group banned in Russia whose founder, the blogger Vladislav Pozdnyakov, says it no longer exists and denies any involvement. Many European officials link the disruption to Europe's support for Ukraine and accuse Moscow of running a destabilisation campaign, which Russia denies. The wave adds to a string of sabotage attributed to hybrid operations, targeting German substations, Baltic defence sites and Leipzig airport.

keys.title: Country after country
keys.text: Czech police counted threats against nine flights from Prague, and a Wizz Air flight to Rome was diverted to Venice. Danish police report threats against Copenhagen airport.

keys.title: Why Ireland matters
keys.text: Dublin is due to host a major European meeting on relations between Russia and Ukraine next week. RTÉ was among the first newsrooms to be targeted.

essentials.title: Haiti's 400 Mawozo gang reaches out to the state as Salvadoran troops close in
essentials.standfirst: Wilson Joseph's gang says it has contacted the national disarmament commission and wants UN mediation. The prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, has announced the killing of a gang leader in Cité Soleil.
body: On Friday 6 November the 400 Mawozo gang, led by Wilson Joseph, told the Associated Press that it had contacted Haiti's national commission for disarmament, demobilisation and reintegration in the name of “peace” and “national reconciliation”.

Accused by the UN and human-rights groups of rape, murder and kidnapping, which it denies, the gang fears an offensive by the more than 2,000 Salvadoran soldiers deployed in recent weeks, and El Salvador's president, Nayib Bukele, has promised to destroy its leader's house.

The same day the prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, announced the death of a gang leader in Cité Soleil, identified by police as the head of the Boston gang, while the disarmament commission says it is following the government's road map.

analysis.title: El Salvador's gamble
analysis.text: The arrival of Salvadoran troops has shifted the balance of power in Port-au-Prince. According to the UN, most of them operate outside the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force, which works with the police, the Haitian army and Vectus Global, a private security firm founded by Erik Prince. Their deployment followed the disappearance of four Salvadoran aviation technicians, and they were attacked on 18 October in gang-held territory. The overture by 400 Mawozo, which is asking for operations to be suspended in some areas and invokes the Geneva Conventions, looks like an attempt to protect itself. The gang says disarmament is “a process” and wants an end to “international interference” in return.

keys.title: Nayib Bukele's reply
keys.text: Challenged on social media over a photo said to show Wilson Joseph's house, El Salvador's president asked for the exact address so that he could destroy it. His government has not commented on the gang's initiative.

keys.title: A country with no elected president
keys.text: Since the Transitional Presidential Council stood down on 7 February, the prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, has led the executive alone. He hailed the Cité Soleil operation on X.

brief.text: The former president, Santiago Peña, removed from office on Friday, was remanded in custody at a military facility on Saturday on the orders of Judge Humberto Otazú, who is pursuing him for breach of trust over the Ueno bank affair.
Iran is negotiating with Moscow to buy the S-400 air-defence system, according to the Telegraph, after a visit to the Kremlin by Mohsen Rezaei, bearing a message from the Supreme Leader.
America's Central Command is offering up to $20m, through the State Department's Rewards for Justice programme, for information on Iran's nuclear programme.
